title: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
seo_title: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 11)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants
standard_text: Photosynthesis as a means of autotrophic nutrition; site of photosynthesis, pigments involved in photosynthesis (elementary idea); photochemical and biosynthetic phases of photosynthesis; cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation; chemiosmotic hypothesis; photorespiration; C₃ and C₄ pathways; factors affecting photosynthesis.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 11 Photosynthesis in Higher Plants: early experiments, pigments, light reactions, photosystems, the Calvin cycle, C₄ plants, photorespiration and limiting factors. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Light reactions make ATP, NADPH and O₂; the Calvin cycle uses them to fix CO₂.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts. In the light reactions on the thylakoids, PS II and PS I absorb light, water is split (giving O₂), and ATP and NADPH are made by non-cyclic photophosphorylation; ATP forms by chemiosmosis.

The Calvin cycle in the stroma fixes CO₂ onto RuBP with RuBisCO; the first product is 3-PGA, and each CO₂ needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. C₄ plants such as maize first fix CO₂ into oxaloacetate with PEP carboxylase and have Kranz anatomy, so they waste little energy on photorespiration.

Example

First product of C₃ cycle?

3 carbons

Answer: PGA

Example

ATP per CO₂ fixed?

3 ATP + 2 NADPH

Answer: 3

Common mistakes

  • Saying the oxygen comes from CO₂.
  • Putting the Calvin cycle in the thylakoids.
  • Calling wheat a C₄ plant.

faq.q: Where does the oxygen released in photosynthesis come from?
faq.a: From the splitting of water (photolysis) in PS II.

faq.q: Why are C₄ plants more efficient in hot, bright places?
faq.a: They concentrate CO₂ around RuBisCO in bundle-sheath cells, so photorespiration hardly happens.
